HISTORY AND PHYSICAL (H&P)

History:
• Main complaint: Progressive fatigue with difficulty getting up in the morning, low daytime energy, and reduced appetite.  
• Onset/duration: Began roughly 2 months ago, coinciding with a new job.  
• Course/progression: Symptoms persistent; no noted improvement.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Poor sleep/insomnia.  
  – Difficulty concentrating; feeling distracted.  
  – Low mood; decreased libido.  
  – Shortness of breath during sports compared with baseline a few months ago.  
• Denies: Suicidal ideation, self-harm thoughts, visual changes.  
• Triggers/relievers: None identified.  
• Previous episodes: None reported.

Past Medical History:
• Hypothyroidism (on levothyroxine).  
• No prior mental-health diagnoses.  
• Surgical/hospitalization history: Not discussed.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Medications: Levothyroxine – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Family history: Father died by suicide ~15 years ago; otherwise non-contributory.

Physical Examination:
(Note: Tele-consultation; no in-person exam performed.)  
• General: Patient alert, oriented, conversant.  
• Reported: No vision changes, no throat swelling.

Impression:
Fatigue with low mood and decreased libido in a patient with known hypothyroidism – differential includes sub-optimally treated hypothyroidism, depressive disorder, and anemia or other medical causes.

Management Plan:
• Arrange in-person GP appointment within the next few days for full physical examination.  
• Order blood work: thyroid function tests, CBC, metabolic panel, ferritin/B-12, and other relevant labs.  
• Discussed mood symptoms; patient denies suicidality but advised to seek help immediately if thoughts of self-harm arise.  
• Reassurance provided that further assessment will clarify cause and guide treatment.

Patient Summary:
Adult male with treated hypothyroidism reports 2 months of increasing fatigue, poor sleep, low mood, reduced libido, and exertional dyspnea. No safety concerns identified. Plan is in-person review and targeted blood tests to evaluate thyroid status and other medical/psychiatric contributors.

Key Takeaways:
• Book face-to-face GP appointment this week for examination and labs.  
• Have thyroid and routine blood tests done; results will direct next steps.  
• Seek urgent help if mood worsens or suicidal thoughts develop.

Next Steps:
• Complete ordered blood tests before GP visit if possible.  
• Review lab results and adjust levothyroxine or initiate mental-health support as indicated.  
• Follow-up appointment after results (within 1–2 weeks).
